Key observations from test image:
- Green corn leaf with distinct lesions
- Elongated/spindle-shaped lesion mid-left: tan/straw center with dark reddish-brown borders
- Broader irregular tan-brown lesion near top
- No pustules, no powdery coating, no black stromata
- Lesions appear to run parallel to leaf veins

Top candidates: **Northern_corn_leaf_blight**, **Anthracnose_leaf_spot_top_dieback**, **Holcus_spot**. Let me view reference images.

The NCLB shows large cigar-shaped lesions, Anthracnose shows oval lesions with dark borders and yellow halos, Holcus shows small round spots - not matching well. Let me check Gray_leaf_spot and Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight too.

Now I have enough reference data to compare. Let me analyze:

**Test image features:**
- Elongated spindle/diamond-shaped lesions running parallel to leaf veins
- Tan/straw-colored centers with distinct dark reddish-brown borders
- Moderate-sized lesions on an otherwise green leaf
- No pustules, no powdery coating, no black dots, no yellow halos

**Comparison:**
- **NCLB**: Elongated cigar/spindle shapes, tan center to darker brown/reddish-brown borders running parallel to veins — matches well
- **Anthracnose leaf spot**: More oval/diamond with very dark (near-black) borders, often with prominent yellow halos — the halos are absent in test image
- **Gray leaf spot**: Strictly rectangular, very linear, vein-bounded — doesn't match the spindle shape
- **Southern Corn Leaf Blight**: Rectangular-to-oval tan spots, more uniform tan color — less distinctive borders
- **Holcus spot**: Small circular spots — doesn't match

The elongated spindle shape with tan/straw center transitioning to darker reddish-brown borders, running parallel to veins, is most consistent with **Northern Corn Leaf Blight** per the description: *"elongated, spindle- or elliptical-shaped necrotic spots...tan/grayish-brown in the center to darker brown or reddish-brown borders."*

Unlike Anthracnose (which has near-black borders and prominent yellow halos), Gray leaf spot (strictly rectangular), or Southern Corn Leaf Blight (more uniform tan without sharp borders), these lesions match the NCLB description of cigar/spindle-shaped necrotic spots with tan centers transitioning to reddish-brown margins."}
